text:
anya patel: Quick RFC follow-up: propose we add an automated "telemetry-driven rollback" lane for quant profiles. idea: if degradation signals (deg_score, sample_bleed) exceed thresholds for a model slice for N minutes, runtime auto-falls back to higher-precision and a patch is created for the descriptor. thoughts?
derek wu: interesting. two big questions: 1) what thresholds do we use (absolute vs delta)? 2) who gets notified / can opt-out per-customer?
anya patel: start with delta-based thresholds to account for per-endpoint baselines. e.g. deg_score_delta>0.15 over 5m AND error_rate_delta>0.02 -> trigger. notifications: create an ops alert + annotate model audit log and send a service patch marked "auto-rollback". customer opt-out via descriptor flag `allow_auto_rollback=false`.
marco silva: one nit: automatic patch creation is powerful but risky. need a dry-run mode where we only simulate the rollback and produce a candidate descriptor for review. maybe require 2 canary confirmations before full patch promoted.
anya patel: agree. propose flow: detect -> simulate rollback (dry-run telemetry) -> if simulated QoS + quality pass for canary traffic (10% by default) then auto-promote after 30m. otherwise keep in sim and notify.
derek wu: hysteresis mechanics? avoid flip-flopping during noisy signals. we should require a cool-down (e.g. 1h) and progressive backoffs: 1st auto-rollback ttl=30m, 2nd=2h, 3rd=24h before manual. also track event_count per-slice.
anya patel: adding hysteresis fields to descriptor/negotiation protocol: `hysteresis_window_ms`, `min_event_count`, `cooldown_ms`, `max_auto_promotions`. runtime will record `last_auto_action_ts` in telemetry.
marco silva: KV cache interaction: if rollback changes precision (e.g. fp8 -> int8) and cache layout differs, we must either invalidate cache or run compatibility shim. auto-rollback must prefer cache-compatible target if cache_hot. otherwise we schedule cache flush during low-traffic window.
derek wu: ops: make sure auto-generated patches have TTL and are labeled `source:auto`. ops dashboard filters should show these separately. also rate-limit to 1 auto-patch per model per hour by default.
ops-bot: Alert rule created: `quant_auto_rollback_rate` -> fires when >1 auto-patch per model within 1h.
anya patel: telemetry contract sketch: events: `quant.suggested_rollback` (with reason tags), `quant.simulation_result` (pass/fail, expected_qos_ms), `quant.auto_patch` (origin, target_precision, ttl). sample payload example included in spec PR.
marco silva: testing: add synthetic drift tests in CI where we inject deg_score shifts and assert simulation metrics + noisy-hysteresis protection.
derek wu: security/approval: any auto-patch must require final approval flag for enterprise customers who opted out of auto changes. we need a per-tenant override.
anya patel: action items: I'll add spec + state machine, include sample config with `allow_auto_rollback`, `hysteresis_*`, `cache_preference`. Derek will draft ops dashboard filters and rate-limits. Marco will add synthetic tests.
marco silva: +1. quick question: do we expose manual revert from console for auto-patches? should be a first-class button labeled "revert auto-rollback" and create a rollback patch with `source:manual`.
derek wu: yes and log the operator id.
anya patel: ok aiming for canary next Tuesday. thanks :rocket:
